findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body: After callers invoke the returned cleanup function, the message handler remains subscribed. Subsequent messages still invoke torn-down callbacks, while repeated attach/dispose cycles accumulate listeners, retained state, and duplicate processing.

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the interval when polling stops
findings.body: The returned stop function no longer cancels the interval. Polling therefore continues indefinitely after teardown, repeated lifecycles accumulate timers, and the active timer can prevent a Node.js process from exiting.

findings.title: [P1] Restore listener removal in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer unregisters the `"message"` handler. Any later socket message invokes callbacks after teardown, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and retained state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Cancel the interval when polling is stopped
findings.body:
Calling the returned stop function leaves the interval active. After teardown, `refresh` continues running every second indefinitely; in Node.js the referenced timer can also prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore removal of the message listener in the disposer
findings.body:
Any caller invoking the returned cleanup function still leaves `handler` subscribed. Subsequent messages trigger callbacks after teardown, and repeated attach/cleanup cycles accumulate duplicate listeners and retained state.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Clear the interval when polling is disposed
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer stops polling. `refresh` continues indefinitely after teardown, and in Node.js the referenced interval can prevent process termination.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore removal of the message listener in the disposer
findings.body:
Calling the returned cleanup function no longer detaches `handler`. Any attach/dispose lifecycle on a long-lived socket retains the handler and captured state; repeated cycles accumulate listeners and duplicate message processing linearly.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Restore cancellation of the polling interval
findings.body:
After any `startPolling` call, the returned disposer cannot stop the interval. The callback continues running every second indefinitely, repeated lifecycles accumulate timers and work, and in Node.js the referenced interval can prevent process shutdown.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
